newsitem.title: EGYPT: Israel wants to kill peace - Palestinian official.
newsitem.headline: Israel wants to kill peace - Palestinian official.

text.p: A senior Palestinian official said on Wednesday Israel's building of a Jewish settlement in the disputed city of Jerusalem was a bid to kill the peace process.

"What is going on on Jabal Abu Ghneim is an Israeli attempt to use violence, tanks and bulldozers to kill the peace process and besiege Jerusalem and Bethlehem," said Nabil Shaath, who is Minister of International Cooperation in the Palestinian Authority (PA).

"The peace process is facing a very dangerous battle...it is aimed at the Judaisation of Jerusalem and take control over Palestinian lands before the final status negotiations," he told reporters after meeting Egypt's Foreign Minister Amr Moussa.

The decision by Israel to build 6,500 homes for Jews on the hillside between Jerusalem and Bethlehem was a blow to the Palestinians, who regard Arab East Jerusalem as the capital of a future state and say the construction precludes planned talks on the city's status.
They say the settlement will change the demographic status of the city before the final negotiations which were supposed to begin on Monday.
Shaath said that the project was just one of the ways Israel was "drawing a new map" of the area it wanted to enforce at the final status talks.
"The problem is not just the settlement of Jabal Abu Ghneim. The Israeli government took a decision on Tuesday to build a new settlement to block the road leading northeast to Jerusalem," he said.
The site is also known in Israel as Har Homa and the construction project, which is in its second day, has sparked international condemnation.
He added that the Israeli authorities had also confiscated within the past few days large amounts of land around Jerusalem, and were evacuating the remaining Palestinians in the area.
